rows.answer: When the cell ahead is taken, a robot: queues for up to 20 ticks if the robot ahead is working (picking, dropping or charging); otherwise replans around nearby robots after 2 blocked ticks; steps aside into a free neighbouring cell after 4-7 blocked ticks, to break a standoff. [WM-6.2]
rows.reference: It queues up to 20 ticks if the robot ahead is working; otherwise it replans around nearby robots after 2 blocked ticks and steps aside into a free neighbouring cell after 4-7 blocked ticks.

rows.answer: Thresholds: Level Threshold What happens Low below 20 % The robot receives no new orders and drives to the nearest free charging bay Critical below 10 % Operator action required (SOP-02) Level Threshold What happens Top-up below 70 % When no orders are waiting, idle robots below 70 % top up at a free charger Charged 95 % Charging stops and the robot returns to parking [RM-4.2]
rows.reference: Below 20 % the robot receives no new orders and drives to the nearest free charging bay; no operator action is needed while it is on its way (SOP-01).

rows.answer: Thresholds: Level Threshold What happens Low below 20 % The robot receives no new orders and drives to the nearest free charging bay Critical below 10 % Operator action required (SOP-02) Level Threshold What happens Top-up below 70 % When no orders are waiting, idle robots below 70 % top up at a free charger Charged 95 % Charging stops and the robot returns to parking [RM-4.2]
rows.reference: Below 10 % operator action is required - pause the robot if it could block an aisle or lane, reassign its order, tow it to the nearest charger, resume it once docked, and record the robot ID as a possible battery fault.

rows.answer: An operator may close an aisle on request ("avoid Aisle 7"). Closing an aisle is only allowed when no robot or person is inside it and no robot is about to pick from it; otherwise pause the robots concerned first (SOP-05). [SAF-3.6]
rows.reference: No. An aisle may only be closed when no robot or person is inside and no robot is about to pick from it; wait until the robot has left, or pause it and reassign its order first.

rows.answer: To stop the whole fleet, press the red E-STOP button at the top of any screen. One press, no confirmation: every robot holds where it is (no driving, picking or dropping, no new orders) and a red banner shows the stop on every screen. Anyone logged in may press it. Use it when a person is injured or in danger, when there is a fire alarm, or when several robots behave abnormally at the same time. [SAF-4.2]
rows.reference: Pause the simulation so all robots stop at once - for an injury, a fire alarm, or several robots behaving abnormally.

rows.answer: Five fault types are monitored. Each is logged as a ROBOT_FAULT event and cleared with a FAULT_CLEARED event. Fault What the robot does Typical duration Main signals battery_spike Battery level drops suddenly by 12-30 % short (about 10 ticks) large negative battery step speed_degradation Drives at half speed 40-120 ticks low movement rate while it has a route stop_event Stops completely (status FAULT) 15-60 ticks no movement, status FAULT route_deviation Leaves its route and wanders to a nearby cell before resuming 20-50 ticks route length grows, detour overheating Motor heats far above normal, then throttles 60-160 ticks of heating, plus cool-down temperature above 60 C, rising [RM-6.1]
rows.reference: Its route length grows instead of shrinking while it leaves the planned route (route deviation).

rows.answer: Traffic also causes stops and slow progress. Before calling a fault, check whether the robot is blocked by other robots, a worker, a closed aisle or a floor hazard (blocked-tick counter, zone congestion). [MG-1.3]
rows.reference: Check whether it is blocked by other robots, a worker, a closed aisle or a floor hazard (blocked-tick counter, zone congestion) before calling a fault.

rows.answer: Action: if the battery is now below 20 %, the robot goes to charge automatically. Note the robot ID. Two spikes on the same robot within a shift: take it out of service and inspect the battery pack and connectors. [MG-2.2]
rows.reference: Take it out of service and inspect the battery pack and connectors.

rows.answer: Symptom: the robot moves at about half speed although its route is free. [MG-3.1]
rows.reference: Its motor temperature; above 60 C it is thermal throttling (see MG-6), otherwise suspect a drive-wheel or encoder problem.
